audience: Replit is for people who want the editor, the hosting, and the agent in one cloud IDE. Students, teachers, and developers who refuse to install a toolchain are the obvious fit. The verdict prices the decision: Core is $20 a month, or $18 if you pay annually. If you only need a generated UI, you do not need this whole environment.

It is a weaker fit when the agent bill is open-ended. Paid agent work is effort-priced and can add up. Core includes $20 toward stronger models, and those credits do not roll over. A spiky month can cost more than the seat.
features: Starter is free. The dollar amount is not printed on the docs page we used, so the table says Free and does not invent $0 as a separate researched figure beyond that word. Core and Pro prices are the cards on replit.com/pricing. Core is $20 a month, or $18 billed annually. Pro is $100 a month, or $90 billed annually. Enterprise is custom.

Hosting and the agent are in the same place. That is the pro that justifies the product against a local editor plus a separate host. Yearly billing is about 10% off, which is how $20 becomes $18 and $100 becomes $90. We are reading those pairs off the cards, not applying a generic discount.
Core includes $20 toward stronger models. The included amount matches the monthly price, which is a useful coincidence and also a ceiling. When it is gone, effort-priced agent work is extra.
limitations: Core credits do not roll over. A quiet month does not stockpile the $20 of model credit. If your agent use is bursty, Pro at $100, or $90 annually, is the plan to read before you assume Core will stretch.
Paid agent work is effort-priced. We do not have a per-task dollar rate in the data, so we will not invent one. The warning is the point: the seat is not a cap on the agent.
The rating is Depends. The IDE is convenient. The agent meter is the condition. Depends means try Starter, buy Core if $20 is the budget, and watch the effort pricing.

faqs.q: How much is Replit Core if I pay yearly?
faqs.a: Core is $18 a month billed annually, against $20 month-to-month. Pro is $90 a month billed annually, against $100. That is the about 10% yearly discount, taken from the cards, not calculated as a new price.
No. Core includes $20 toward stronger models, and those credits do not roll over. A quiet month does not bank them.

Because the IDE and hosting are genuinely convenient at $20, and the agent is effort-priced on top. The seat is not the whole bill.
